title: Local dimension bound for ordinary modifications and their centers
statement: Let $A$ be a reduced Noetherian local ring of finite Krull dimension $n$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], where reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent. Let $P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a finite tower of ordinary blowups in coherent nowhere dense centers [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent]. Then $P$ is reduced and Noetherian, has dimension at most $n$, and every reduced nowhere dense closed subscheme $W\subset P$ has dimension at most $n-1$ when $n\ge1$. In particular all local rings of $W$ have dimension at most $n-1$. The empty subscheme is allowed. For a reduced Noetherian scheme $X$, a point $x$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=n$, and such a tower over $X$, the same bounds hold after base change to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$. If $X$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], its local schemes, the resulting blowup schemes, and their reduced closed subschemes are quasi-excellent as well. Thus these local schemes are objects of the reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent category over $\mathbf Q$ whenever $X$ is over $\mathbf Q$.

No Stacks tag states this combined assertion. Quasi-excellence under localization and finite type: Stacks Tag 07QU, more-algebra.tex, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent (quasi-excellent alternative).

proof.text: Write the tower as $P_m\to\cdots\to P_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], $P_0$ is reduced, and its single affine chart is Noetherian. Induct on $i$: [lem-per-reduced-noetherian-blowup-geometry] applied to the coherent center of $P_{i+1}\to P_i$ gives a reduced Noetherian $P_{i+1}$ and a finite-type arrow. The base case is $i=0$; induction reaches every stage, including a tower of length zero. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], the composite $P_m\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finite type.

source.place: Tags 0808, lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme, and 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective; induction on the number of blowups.

proof.text: For each arrow, the ordinary-blowup clause of [lem-per-noetherian-normalized-blowup-finality] gives a bijection on component generic points with isomorphic residue fields: its hypotheses are reducedness and local Noetherianness from Step 1, and the given finite-type nowhere dense center. Compose those bijections and residue-field isomorphisms along the finite tower. Thus every component generic point of $P_m$ maps to a component generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with transcendence degree zero. By [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $\dim\operatorname{Spec}A=n$. Apply [lem-sfb-generic-residue-transcendence-dimension-bound] with $d=n$ and generic transcendence bound $0$ to the finite-type composite from Step 1. It gives $\dim P_m\leq n$. This uses the inequality form of the dimension formula, which requires no catenarity.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, with all generic transcendence degrees zero; generic points of ordinary blowups: divisors.tex, Tag 0BFM, lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components.

proof.text: Let $W\subset P_m$ be nowhere dense and closed. By [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], any chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_e$ in $W$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $P_m$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], $Z_e$ lies in a component $C$ of $P_m$. Since $P_m$ is Noetherian (Step 1), it has finitely many components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], so $C$ minus the union of the other components is a nonempty open subset of $P_m$; nowhere-density of $W$ therefore gives $C\not\subseteq W$, so $Z_e\subsetneq C$ appends one strict inclusion. Hence $e+1\leq n$ by Step 2, and $\dim W\leq n-1$ for $n\geq1$. The empty case has no chains and dimension $-\infty$. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], every $\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}\leq\dim W$. When $n=0$ the same argument forces $W$ empty.

source.place: Definition of Krull dimension by irreducible closed chains; append a component to a chain in a nowhere dense closed subset. Local-ring consequence: properties.tex, Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension.

proof.text: For the scheme formulation put $L=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}L$. Choose an affine neighborhood $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ of $x$, with prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$; then $L=R_{\mathfrak p}$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and $L$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is reduced by the definition [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [lem-sbc-canonical-stalk-spectrum-flat], $S\to X$ is flat; therefore every stage projection $P_i\times_XS\to P_i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: Tag 01U9, lemma-base-change-flat; stalk-spectrum morphism is a localization on affine neighborhoods.

proof.text: At each stage of the tower on $X$, let $U_i$ be the complement of the center. It is dense by hypothesis. Its open immersion is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc] and quasi-separated (its diagonal is an isomorphism). Since $P_i$ is reduced by the induction of Step 1 applied over $X$, [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] says its scheme-theoretic image is $P_i$. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to the flat projection of Step 4. The pulled-back open is schematically, hence topologically, dense, so the pulled-back center is nowhere dense. The comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]; thus the pulled-back arrow is the ordinary blowup of the extended center ideal. On affine charts the images of finitely many generators generate that extended ideal, which is quasi-coherent of finite type. Starting with the Noetherian $S$, the ordinary-blowup induction of Step 1 keeps all pulled-back stages Noetherian; [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes these ideals coherent at each inductive step. Consequently the base-changed tower satisfies the initial hypotheses over $L$, of dimension $n$. Steps 1--3 applied to this tower prove precisely the stated local bounds. A center may pull back to the empty subscheme; its unit ideal gives an allowed identity stage.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; schematic density under flat base change: morphisms.tex Tag 081I. Finite generators pull back to generators; coherence: coherent.tex Tag 01XZ.

proof.text: Assume now that $X$ is quasi-excellent, imposed on its affine coordinate rings as in the statement. For $L=R_{\mathfrak p}$ of Step 4, [lem-per-quasi-excellent-localization] gives quasi-excellence of $L$. In particular $L$ is a G-ring and J-2 by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Apply [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] and [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] to the single affine cover $S=\operatorname{Spec}L$: every affine open of $S$ has a coordinate ring that is both a G-ring and J-2; it is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] since $S$ is Noetherian, hence it is quasi-excellent. The local Noetherian hypothesis needed for the J-2 result was established in Step 4.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, localization clause. Affine-cover locality of the G-ring and J-2 predicates: morphisms.tex, lemma-characterize-quasi-excellent.

proof.text: Each ordinary blowup arrow is finite type by Step 1. Apply [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] inductively to the tower over $X$, and also to the tower over $S$ using Step 6: all stage schemes are quasi-excellent. A closed immersion has on affine charts a quotient map $B\twoheadrightarrow B/J$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Such an algebra is generated over $B$ by the empty set, so this immersion is locally of finite type. Apply the same quasi-excellence stability result to any reduced closed subscheme of any stage. Its hypothesis on the target holds by this induction. Finally, when $X$ is a $\mathbf Q$-scheme, composing structure maps makes $S$, all these stage schemes, and their closed subschemes $\mathbf Q$-schemes. Together with reducedness and Noetherianness from Steps 1 and 4--5 (and the finite-type stability statement for the closed subschemes), these are the asserted objects of the reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent category.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, finite-type clause; closed immersions are affine-locally quotient algebras.

lean.statement: theorem blowup_local_dimension_bound (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [_root_.IsReduced A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (n : ℕ) (hn : ringKrullDim A = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) (T : OrdinaryBlowupTower (Spec (.of A))) (hcoh : ∀ i : Fin T.length, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (T.level i.castSucc).toRingedSpace (T.center i).toModules) (hdense : ∀ i : Fin T.length, IsNowhereDense ((T.center i).support : Set (T.level i.castSucc))) : IsReduced (T.level (Fin.last T.length)) ∧ IsNoetherian (T.level (Fin.last T.length)) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (T.level (Fin.last T.length)) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∀ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ T.level (Fin.last T.length)) [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsReduced W], IsNowhereDense (Set.range j) → 1 ≤ n → topologicalKrullDim W ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∀ w : W, ringKrullDim (W.presheaf.stalk w) ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
